root_cause: Fa0/2 is still in default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10, splitting PC1 and PC2 into different broadcast domains.
evidence: show vlan brief lists Fa0/2 under VLAN1, not VLAN10; show run int fa0/2 confirms 'switchport access vlan 1'.
fix_steps_json: ["interface fa0/2", "switchport access vlan 10", "confirm with show vlan brief", "re-test ping PC1 to PC2"]

root_cause: VLAN 30 was assigned to ports but never created with the global 'vlan 30' command, so the ports are inactive.
evidence: show vlan brief has no VLAN30 entry at all even though fa0/5 is configured with 'switchport access vlan 30'.
fix_steps_json: ["vlan 30 (global config)", "name Sales", "exit", "confirm VLAN30 now shows ACTIVE", "re-test connectivity between the two ports"]

root_cause: The trunk between SW1 and SW2 is not carrying VLAN 20 at all, so VLAN 20 traffic never crosses the link.
evidence: Both switches show VLAN20 configured locally; assumed the trunk's allowed-VLAN list excludes VLAN 20.
fix_steps_json: ["check switchport trunk allowed vlan on both ends", "add vlan 20 to the allowed list if missing", "re-test VLAN 20 connectivity across the trunk"]

root_cause: Fa0/8 was never assigned to VLAN 40 and is sitting in default VLAN 1.
evidence: show vlan brief places fa0/8 under VLAN1; show run int fa0/8 has no access vlan command.
fix_steps_json: ["interface fa0/8", "switchport access vlan 40", "confirm with show vlan brief", "re-test printer reachability"]

root_cause: Router subinterface Gi0/0.10 (the VLAN 10 gateway) is administratively shut down.
evidence: show ip interface brief shows Gi0/0.10 administratively down; show run confirms a 'shutdown' line under that subinterface.
fix_steps_json: ["interface Gi0/0.10", "no shutdown", "confirm status is up/up", "re-test connectivity from VLAN 10 to other VLANs"]

root_cause: PC3's default gateway (192.168.6.1) is on a different subnet than the router's real interface (192.168.5.1).
evidence: PC3 ipconfig gateway is 192.168.6.1 while R1 Gi0/1 is 192.168.5.1/24.
fix_steps_json: ["reconfigure PC3's gateway to 192.168.5.1", "if via DHCP, fix the default-router option on the pool", "re-test off-subnet connectivity"]

root_cause: The laptop's gateway address has a typo (172.16.1.001) and never matches the router's real interface (172.16.1.1).
evidence: Laptop ipconfig shows gateway 172.16.1.001 vs router Gi0/0 at 172.16.1.1.
fix_steps_json: ["correct the static gateway to 172.16.1.1", "or switch the laptop to DHCP", "re-test connectivity beyond the local subnet"]

root_cause: Branch router Gi0/1, the LAN gateway interface, is line-protocol down.
evidence: show ip int brief reports Gi0/1 down/down; log shows %LINK-3-UPDOWN changed state to down.
fix_steps_json: ["check the physical cable/SFP on Gi0/1", "reseat or replace the cable", "no shutdown if administratively disabled", "confirm up/up and re-test LAN connectivity"]

root_cause: PC5's default gateway address is wrong; it should point at 192.168.20.1 like the router interface shows.
evidence: PC5's gateway differs from what the router reports for that segment.
fix_steps_json: ["reconfigure PC5's gateway to match the router interface", "re-test connectivity"]

root_cause: The DHCP scope for VLAN 50 is fully leased out (50/50), so new clients fall back to APIPA.
evidence: show ip dhcp pool LAB50 reports leased 50 of 50; debug shows DHCPDISCOVER with no addresses available.
fix_steps_json: ["enlarge the DHCP pool's address range", "or shorten the lease time to recycle stale leases", "clear expired bindings with clear ip dhcp binding *", "re-test that new clients receive an address"]

root_cause: The router's own gateway address (10.10.60.1) was never excluded from the DHCP pool and got leased to a client.
evidence: show ip dhcp binding shows 10.10.60.1 leased to a client MAC; no ip dhcp excluded-address command is present for it.
fix_steps_json: ["ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.60.1 10.10.60.10", "clear the bad lease with clear ip dhcp binding 10.10.60.1", "re-test that the client gets a different address"]

root_cause: VLAN 70's gateway interface is missing 'ip helper-address', so DHCP broadcasts never reach the remote server.
evidence: show run int vlan70 has no ip helper-address line; debug shows no DHCPDISCOVER arriving at the server interface.
fix_steps_json: ["interface vlan70", "ip helper-address <dhcp-server-ip>", "re-test that VLAN 70 clients receive a lease"]

root_cause: Clients on VLAN 80 are not receiving any default gateway from DHCP at all.
evidence: Browsing fails after clients get an IP, suggesting a gateway or DNS problem in the DHCP scope.
next_command: show run | section dhcp pool LAB80
fix_steps_json: ["review the DHCP pool configuration for LAB80", "verify the default-router and dns-server options"]

root_cause: The internal DNS server at 10.10.1.53 is unreachable, so name resolution fails even though the target service's IP is fine.
evidence: Ping to 10.10.1.53 times out while ping to the web server's IP succeeds.
fix_steps_json: ["check the DNS server's power/interface status", "verify routing/ACLs toward 10.10.1.53", "restart the DNS service if the host is reachable but not answering on port 53", "re-test nslookup"]

root_cause: This PC's statically configured DNS server IP has a digit transposition (10.10.1.35 instead of 10.10.1.53).
evidence: ipconfig /all shows DNS 10.10.1.35, which is unreachable, while the correct server is 10.10.1.53.
fix_steps_json: ["correct the static DNS entry to 10.10.1.53", "or switch the PC back to DHCP-assigned DNS", "re-test nslookup"]

root_cause: A newly added ACL entry on the WAN link denies UDP port 53, blocking DNS while ICMP still passes.
evidence: show access-lists WAN-IN shows 'deny udp any any eq 53' ahead of the permit statements; ping still succeeds, isolating this to port 53 specifically.
fix_steps_json: ["remove or reorder the deny udp eq 53 line", "add an explicit permit for udp any any eq 53 if DNS should be allowed", "re-test nslookup from the branch"]

root_cause: No DNS A record exists for the new app server, so the hostname simply does not resolve.
evidence: nslookup returns non-existent domain and the DNS zone has no A record for appserver.
next_command: show zone internal.local (or check DNS server console)
fix_steps_json: ["create an A record for appserver.local pointing to 10.10.9.30", "re-test nslookup", "re-test browsing by hostname"]

root_cause: HQ is missing the static route to the branch LAN subnet 172.20.5.0/24, so return traffic has nowhere to go.
evidence: HQ show ip route has no entry for 172.20.5.0/24; the corresponding ip route statement is absent from the running config.
fix_steps_json: ["ip route 172.20.5.0 255.255.255.0 <branch-wan-ip>", "confirm the route appears in show ip route", "re-test ping from HQ to a branch LAN host"]

root_cause: OSPF is not enabled on the R1-R2 link interface, so no neighbor relationship ever forms.
evidence: show ip ospf neighbor is empty on R1, suggesting OSPF is not running on that interface.
fix_steps_json: ["confirm the interface is included in the OSPF network statement or has 'ip ospf 1 area 0' applied", "re-test neighbor formation"]

root_cause: The default route's next-hop IP (203.0.113.254) is wrong; the real ISP hand-off is 203.0.113.253.
evidence: Ping to the configured next hop 203.0.113.254 times out, indicating that address does not answer on the WAN link.
fix_steps_json: ["update the static route: ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.253", "remove the old incorrect static route", "re-test internet reachability"]

root_cause: A policy-based routing map is sending return traffic out a misconfigured interface, causing asymmetric routing.
evidence: Traceroute A-to-B is clean but B-to-A dies at the last hop; the route-map POLICY forces the return path onto a different interface.
fix_steps_json: ["review the route-map's match/set statements for the return direction", "correct the set interface/next-hop to match the intended path", "re-test bidirectional traceroute"]

root_cause: The new PAYROLL-IN ACL only permits TCP 443, so the app's real port (8443) is caught by the implicit deny.
evidence: show access-lists PAYROLL-IN only has a permit for eq 443; hit counters show the implicit deny incrementing heavily.
fix_steps_json: ["add: permit tcp 10.10.11.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.10.99.5 eq 8443", "re-test HR access to the payroll app", "confirm implicit-deny hit counter stops climbing"]

root_cause: The ACL is missing a deny statement for host 10.10.12.50 entirely, which is why it still gets through.
evidence: show access-lists BLOCK-HOST lists a permit for the subnet; assumed the specific deny line was never added.
fix_steps_json: ["add a deny statement for host 10.10.12.50 to the ACL", "re-test that the host is now blocked"]

root_cause: The LAB-ACL is applied in the wrong direction ('out' instead of 'in') on the VLAN 90 interface.
evidence: show run int vlan90 shows 'ip access-group LAB-ACL out', but the ACL's permit rules are written for inbound HTTP.
fix_steps_json: ["remove: ip access-group LAB-ACL out", "add: ip access-group LAB-ACL in", "re-test inbound HTTP to the test server from outside"]

root_cause: ACL 101 is a stateless list that only permits outbound DNS queries and has no matching entry for return traffic, so responses are dropped.
evidence: show access-lists 101 shows only 'permit udp 10.10.13.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 53' with nothing allowing the reply traffic back in.
fix_steps_json: ["add a permit for udp any eq 53 10.10.13.0 0.0.0.255 on the return leg, or replace with a reflexive/extended ACL that tracks established sessions", "re-test DNS resolution from VLAN 13"]

root_cause: 'ip nat inside' and 'ip nat outside' were never applied to the LAN and WAN interfaces, so the NAT rule has nothing to act on.
evidence: show ip interface shows neither Gi0/1 nor Gi0/0 marked with a NAT role, even though the overload rule exists in the config.
fix_steps_json: ["interface Gi0/1 / ip nat inside", "interface Gi0/0 / ip nat outside", "re-test internet access from an internal host", "confirm entries appear in show ip nat translations"]

root_cause: NAT overload is not enabled at all for this subnet, which is why most hosts cannot reach the internet.
evidence: Only a few hosts show up in show ip nat translations, suggesting NAT overload was never turned on for the subnet.
fix_steps_json: ["verify ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/0 overload is present", "re-test internet access from an affected host"]

root_cause: No static NAT/port-forward rule exists for the internal web server, so inbound requests from outside are never translated.
evidence: show run has no matching 'ip nat inside source static tcp' line for 10.10.5.20; show ip nat translations has no static entry.
fix_steps_json: ["ip nat inside source static tcp 10.10.5.20 80 interface Gi0/0 80", "re-test reaching the server from outside the network", "confirm the static entry appears in show ip nat translations"]

root_cause: The Guest SSID is mapped to VLAN 10 (internal/trusted) instead of the isolated VLAN 99, so guest traffic reaches internal servers.
evidence: show wlan 2 shows 'interface VLAN10' for the Guest SSID, and VLAN10 has no isolation ACL applied.
fix_steps_json: ["remap the Guest SSID's interface to VLAN 99", "confirm VLAN 99 has the guest-isolation ACL applied", "re-test that guest devices cannot reach internal servers"]

root_cause: The RADIUS server's shared secret was recently changed and needs to be updated on the WLC.
evidence: Multiple 802.1X authentication failures were logged, which could point to a RADIUS shared-secret mismatch.
fix_steps_json: ["verify the RADIUS shared secret on the WLC matches the RADIUS server", "re-test authentication from an affected laptop"]
